description: Records as stored at main 873f7d8 (schema 2.12) before the second frontier-governance increment of 2026-10-11: the earlier metadata, the IDs the increment added (Commission guidelines, the training-content template, further chapters of the EU Code, the Signatory Taskforce Vademecum, a draft implementing regulation, the New York Chapter 96 text and a Chinese generative-AI measure) and the rows it changed, as they were: the Code of Practice and New York RAISE Act entities and the New York signing-announcement claim. The test-only historical view removes the added rows and restores the earlier ones.

meta.title: Selekoa historical research sample
meta.scope: Selected historical records, 1965–2024, plus prior roles with unknown dates. Genesis source checks are dated 2026-09-17; personnel-continuity checks are dated 2026-09-18. Human source review pending. Not a current or comprehensive sector inventory. Governance version histories through July 2026, researched September 18, 2026; policy text is not evidence of implementation. Selected capital and compute records through April 2026; transaction stages do not imply current arrangements or realised spending. Targeted corrections dated 2026-09-25: one attributed claim accepted after explicit human source review; a second narrowly scoped résumé passage is human-reviewed. Other seed claims remain pending. Intellectual Lineage II adds selected oversight citations and agenda reception, checked 2026-09-25; all new records remain pending human review. Evaluation Institutions I adds bounded institutional and documentary records, checked 2026-09-27; new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted. Evaluation Ontology I adds four scoped engagement and institutional announcement seeds, checked 2026-09-28; no human acceptance or legal succession inferred. Schema 2.7 records each source's language; the frontier safety framework sources also record the nearest existing Internet Archive capture, checked 2026-10-03. A capture shows only what the archive held on its date and does not authenticate earlier bytes. Schema 2.8 adds quoted framework provisions, recorded absences, provision-level changes and the first contested assessments to the frontier safety frameworks collection, together with Meta and Microsoft framework families, checked 2026-10-03; provisions describe what editions state, not implementation. Schema 2.9 adds control-structure and external-commitment records; its first topic, California SB 53 as chaptered (enactment, 19 quoted provisions and four framework editions that link themselves to it in their own words), was checked 2026-10-04. A commitment or legal obligation is never evidence of compliance, and no record states that the statute applies to a named company. Schema 2.10 records assessments as questions posed by Selekoa rather than statements of a source, and dates an assessment by what it assesses, never by the publication window of its sources (corrected 2026-10-05). Schema 2.11 adds propositions and the first human-thought collection: located texts from 1863 to 2022 that articulate, contest or bear on propositions about machine intelligence, each with its role and register, checked 2026-10-06. "Earliest located" means the earliest text found by the recorded searches; no record claims a first use, an origin or an influence. Schema 2.12 adds a collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s documented arguments about common claims on advanced AI, 1996–2026: dated passages that state, contest or bear on 29 generically phrased propositions, with engagement, retrospective reports and context-only passages marked, admitted 2026-10-08 from a machine-prepared and machine-audited candidate pack. A record says what a text states, not whether it is right. The 2026-10-10 frontier-governance increment adds selected provisions of the EU AI Act as published in 2024 and of the 2026 Digital Omnibus amendments that bear on general-purpose AI model providers, and the New York RAISE Act as announced by the Governor; checked 2026-10-10, new claims remain seeds, not editorially accepted, and Regulation texts describe duties, not compliance.

entities.description: The EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, received and published by the European Commission on 10 July 2025. It consists of three separately authored chapters (Transparency, Copyright, and Safety and Security); the provisions recorded here are quoted from the Safety and Security chapter. Signing it is not evidence of compliance.

entities.name: New York RAISE Act (Responsible AI Safety and Education Act), as described by the Governor
aliases: Responsible AI Safety and Education Act
entities.description: New York legislation on large frontier AI developers. Selekoa has not inspected the bill or session-law text; the record rests on two announcements by the Governor. Bill numbers are those the Governor’s release gives for the chapter amendments.

claims.subject: governor-of-new-york
claims.statement: The Governor of New York announced on 19 December 2025 that she had signed legislation requiring AI frameworks for frontier-model developers, the release names the RAISE Act (S6953B/A6453B) and refers to agreed-upon chapter amendments.

time.note: Date of the Governor’s release (day precision), which says the Governor “today signed”. The signing date and chapter number in the session laws were not inspected.

claims.qualification: An announcement by the Governor’s office about the signing. The bill and session-law text were not retrieved (the legislature’s site refused automated access), so no provision of the statute is recorded; the details in the context evidence are the Governor’s descriptions of the law as of the dated release, not the law’s text. Secondary summaries report an original signing in December 2025 and a later chapter amendment signed on 27 March 2026; no official document giving the March date was located, so how the two events relate is not established, and the penalty figures and thresholds described in the December release may have been changed by later amendment. The Governor’s release of 21 September 2026 says compliance is required beginning January 2027. Signing is not evidence of application to a named developer, compliance or enforcement.
